raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles, $\triangle DCE$ is equilateral, and $\triangle FCG$ is isosceles. Find the measure of $\angle 5$ at vertex $C$.

method.method_draft: Direct right-side triangle route: From the image, read that A, D, F, G, E, B are collinear in that order, C is the apex, angle 5 is the angle between CE and CB, the 42° angle is at A of triangle ABC, and E lies on the same straight base line as D and B. From the text, use that triangle ABC is isosceles with base AB, so the base angles at A and B are equal; hence angle ABC = 42°. Also use that triangle DCE is equilateral, so angle CED = 60°. Since ED and EB are opposite rays on the straight base line, angle CEB = 180° - 60° = 120°. In triangle CEB, compute angle ECB = 180° - 120° - 42° = 18°, which is angle 5.

method.method_draft: Apex decomposition route: From the image, read that the rays CA, CD, CF, CG, CE, CB divide the apex angle ∠ACB into angles 1 through 5, and A, D, F, G, E, B lie on one straight line. The 42° angle is ∠CAB, and angle 5 is the rightmost apex sector between CE and CB. From the text, use that triangle ABC is isosceles with base AB, so ∠ABC = ∠CAB = 42°, giving total apex angle ∠ACB = 180° - 42° - 42° = 96°. Since triangle DCE is equilateral, ∠DCE = angle 2 + angle 3 + angle 4 = 60°. Also, because DCE is equilateral, ∠CDE = 60°; since DA and DE are opposite rays, ∠ADC = 120°. In triangle ACD, ∠CAD = 42° and ∠ADC = 120°, so angle 1 = ∠ACD = 18°. Therefore angle 5 = total ∠ACB - angle 1 - ∠DCE = 96° - 18° - 60° = 18°.
